summary: Both changes tighten the posture: every vendored Codex session drops from full machine access to workspace-write, and the fail-closed hook wiring becomes tamper-evident under the 0009 frozen-gate audit (drift is a pr_ready blocker, named by file). The escape hatch grants nothing programmatically — broader access requires a human-authored, diff-visible config edit, and upgrades revert it. The live sandbox refusal of the worker's own .codex write during this story is direct evidence the workspace-write boundary holds where it matters.
residual_risks: A client can still run a manually-configured full-access Codex session; the harness makes that a visible choice, not an impossibility — the 0041/0030 drift-defense ceiling.
